label: token right after an early t (orig positions 1-2)
explanation: Fires during the original phase on the step right after the letter t is input, but only when that t is at position 0 or 1 (so the feature is on step 1 or 2). It fires on every such step (dev precision 1.0) and these steps carry about 99.7% of the activation mass. Magnitude is highest at step 2 after an x-t prefix (e.g. q t [l], about 2.15 = max). At step 1, after a leading t, it is about 0.75-0.87 of max. It does not fire after a t at position 2 or later (only rare weak activations at t=3), and it does not fire in the delimiter or copy phases even when the copied input is t. The missed activations are tiny, near-zero values, mostly after y or s at early steps.

issues: Minor overclaim: 'does not fire in the delimiter or copy phases' is not literally true. 59 dev copy-phase steps are active, all at t=5 (recall_idx 2), but they carry only 0.02% of the mass. phase==2 scores precision 2e-5.

The misses are systematic but negligible in mass. About 2.9k dev steps fire at step 1 after a leading y (and about 0.5k after s), all at activation ~0.00 relative to max. Together with weak t=3 activations they make up all 4.7k test misses, which hold only 0.3% of the mass. That is why recall is 0.877 while mass recall is 0.997.
t=3 after t: 9.4% of these steps fire, and only weakly (mass 0.26%). Extending the predicate to t<=3 drops test F1 to 0.796, so the original t<=2 cutoff is correct.

Checked: test precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives, test mass recall is 0.997, the top activations are q t [l] at 1.00 (max 2.149), and step-1 activations after a leading t are 0.81-0.87, consistent with the explanation.
